analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Shell Energy Stadium on Saturday 28 November (1:30 pm local), four days after Game 1 in San Jose; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Houston's home league games were low-scoring (19 scored, 15 conceded in 17) and the August meeting here ended 0-0. Guilherme is Houston's main outlet, while San Jose rely on Preston Judd and their goal-scoring centre-backs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I lean lower. Houston's home games this season averaged about two goals in total, the August meeting here was 0-0, and Jonathan Bond tied the club record with 12 clean sheets.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners. I lean higher: Houston won nine corners at home to St. Louis while pressing for a goal, and San Jose conceded eight at Minnesota, so a Houston side at home should win plenty.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. There is little history of bad blood between these two, Houston were booked once on Decision Day and San Jose three times, so I stay with the number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The site expects 25.8 shots. Houston took 23 shots at home to St. Louis, so their home volume is real even when the goals do not come, and I lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 on target and I lean lower. Houston put only six of those 23 shots on target against St. Louis and San Jose managed three at Minnesota, so accuracy rather than volume is the problem for both.
